title: Hosted API — Cost Clarity & Developer Onboard Playbook
content:
TL;DR:
A compact playbook for developer-facing messaging that foregrounds cost transparency and quick time-to-first-success. Focus: reduce billing surprise, shorten first integration to <30m, and give explicit controls (batching, cache, token caps) as product hooks.

Why this matters (problem statement):
- Developers stop integrating when the first unpredictable bill or opaque latency shows up.
- Pricing language that sounds like legalese or abstract rates (e.g., "per-token") doesn't map to engineering decisions (how many calls, what's the latency impact, how to cap spend).
- Competitors either sell simplicity (flat price, low-touch) or enterprise predictability (contracts). We can lead with developer agency: ship quickly, measure cost, then scale predictably.

Core positioning (single-sentence):
- "Hosted API for engineers who want predictable cost and fast integration — ship a prototype in minutes, control spend in production."

Key developer-first value props (short bullets for landing page and hero sections):
- "Ship now, pay how you scale" — clear cost controls and transparent per-token math at the point of integration.
- "From prototype to SLA" — same API across hosted, dedicated, and private; upgrade paths without code changes.
- "No billing surprises" — built-in spend caps, per-route budgets, and dry-run cost estimates for prompt sets.
- "Latency you can count on" — published p95/p99 numbers per model and region with test endpoints.
- "Developer ergonomics" — streaming, function-calling, and SDKs in your stack (examples for Node, Python, Go).

Three quickstart angles (copy + engineer flow):
1) Minimal demo (30 minutes) — "Echo to App"
   - Hook line: "From nothing to a chat-enabled page in 30 minutes."
   - Steps: signup → install SDK → create API key → paste sample chat code → open local page.
   - Pricing message: free starter tokens + real-time cost preview in dev console. 
   - Success metric: dev runs first generate call within 30 minutes; measure time-to-first-token and sample latency.

2) Proof-of-concept (2 days) — "Real prompt, real metrics"
   - Hook: bring your prompt set and demo production-ish cost numbers.
   - Steps: upload 10 prompts (CLI), run dry-run cost calculator, attach a route and set per-route cap, deploy canary.
   - Pricing message: show estimated monthly cost at traffic X and offer an intro 25% commit credit for first month.

3) Early production (weeks) — "Predictable month 1"
   - Hook: migrate a single feature behind a feature flag with spend guardrails.
   - Steps: pin model version, enable KV/prefix cache, configure batching profile, set concurrent request limit, attach SLO window.
   - Pricing message: give a clear convert-to-dedicated threshold (tokens/month) and an accelerator offer for reserved capacity.

Pricing language drafts (experimentable variants):
- Variant A (Engineer math): "$0.0008 / token (input) · $0.0012 / token (output). Example: 50 tokens prompt + 150 tokens response ≈ $0.18 per call."
  - Supporting UI: calculator that accepts batch size & QPS, shows $/hour and $/million tokens.

- Variant B (Predictable starter): "Starter: 200k free tokens/month. Pay-as-you-go after; upgrade to committed credits for predictable pricing and unit discounts."

- Variant C (Safety-first): "Set a per-route cap (USD) and soft alerts. When cap reached, auto-fallback to cheaper model or degraded mode."

Microcopy and CTAs (for docs, emails, console):
- Signup microcopy: "Create an API key — we'll give you 200k free tokens to try things out. No card required for the first 7 days."
- Console banner: "Estimate cost for this prompt set →" (button)
- Billing prompt: "Set a daily cap to prevent runaway bills (suggested: 2x your dev spend)."
- Email subject sample: "Your Redwood test keys are ready — start generating in 5 minutes"

Competitive context (quick notes):
- Competitor X: simple per-call UX but hides long-tail latency + opaque queuing. We can call out: "See the latency profile before you ship."
- Competitor Y: enterprise reserved capacity but heavyweight onboarding. Our edge: easy path to reserved without code changes + dev-first credits to bootstrap.
- OSS runtimes: great for cost but leak ops burden; pitch: "All the control without the ops tax."

Objections & suggested responses (sales/AE & support playbook):
- "I need enterprise SSO and audit logs before sending data." → "Private deployment options and customer-managed KMS are available; we can provision a dedicated environment during pilot."
- "How do I avoid surprise costs from bad prompts?" → "Use per-route caps, dry-run estimator, and token budget alerts; we can also set a global hard cap."
- "Is the hosted model fast enough?" → "We publish model-region p95/p99 and provide a test endpoint to measure latency with your payloads."

Metrics & experiments (what to A/B + success criteria):
- Experiment 1: pricing copy A (explicit math) vs B (starter + upgrade CTA). Metric: conversion from signup → first generate within 72h.
- Experiment 2: cost-estimator CTA in quickstart vs no estimator. Metric: time-to-first-success and drop in support tickets about billing.
- Experiment 3: offering per-route cap default on vs manual setup. Metric: % of users who reach >$10 without hitting cap, and customer satisfaction NPS at day 14.

Console/product hooks to support messaging (engineering asks):
- Dry-run cost calculator: takes prompt set, tokens, batch size, returns estimated monthly spend.
- Per-route budgeting: UI & API to set USD caps, thresholds, and fallback model toggles.
- One-click dev env: preseed SDK snippet with environment key that auto-expands free tokens.
- Latency test endpoint: allow customers to ping and receive p95/p99 for their payload sizes.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Free-tier sizing: 200k tokens seems attractive but could be abused. Do we require email verification or soft throttles?
- Displaying per-token numbers may scare non-technical buyers. Should marketing have a higher-level $/feature example on public pages?
- How aggressive should the default per-route cap be for early production users?

Next steps (who does what):
- Marketing: iterate hero snippets and pricing variants for landing A/B (owner: Sofia).
- Product: spec dry-run calculator + per-route budgets API (owner: Eng-product-sprint).
- Growth/Analytics: instrument funnels: signup → first-key → first-generate → enable-cap (owner: Liam).
- Support: prepare battlecards for top 5 objections and latency benchmark troubleshooting (owner: Noah).

Notes-to-self / messy bits:
- Pull in latency profiles for top 5 models (ask infra to export last 90d p95/p99).
- Draft console banners for the 30-minute demo with links to sample apps (Next: create repo template).
- Consider a "pay as you scale" calculator that projects cost at different QPS and token lengths (could be a top-of-funnel lead gen).

End of draft — feel free to rip pieces for emails, console copy, and a 1-pager for sales.

Unresolved items:
- Final free-tier amount and friction level.
- Exact discount bands for committed credits vs pay-as-you-go.
- Legal review for public pricing examples.
summary: Playbook draft for developer-focused hosted-API messaging: cost clarity, quickstarts, pricing copy variants, experiments and product asks. Goal is reduce billing surprise and accelerate time-to-first-success.
